fullPassage: A study investigated the economic cost of prejudice based on blind assumptions. Researchers gave a group of Danish teenagers the choice of working with one of two people. The teenagers had never met either of them. One of the people had a name that suggested they were from a similar ethnic or religious background to the teenager. The other had a name that suggested they were from a different ethnic or religious background. The study showed that the teenagers were prepared to earn an average of 8% less if they could work with someone they thought came from the same ethnic or religious background. And this prejudice was evident among teenagers with ethnic majority names as well as those with ethnic minority names. The teenagers were blindly making assumptions about the race of their potential colleagues. They then applied prejudice to those assumptions, to the point where they actually allowed that prejudice to reduce their own potential income. The job required the two teenagers to work together for just 90 minutes.

earn 8% less to work with someone from the same background
refuse to work with anyone from a different background
change their religious beliefs to match their colleagues

det.korean: 같은 배경의 사람과 일하기 위해 8% 덜 벌 의향: 편견의 경제적 비용
det.analysis:
❌ ① earn more money by working with diverse colleagues(다양한 동료와 더 벌기): 정반대
✅ ② earn 8% less to work with someone from the same background(같은 배경과 8% 덜 벌기): 핵심 발견 ←정답
❌ ③ refuse to work with anyone from a different background(다른 배경과 일하기 거부): 거부가 아닌 수입 감소 감수
❌ ④ change their religious beliefs to match their colleagues(종교 변경): 맥락 무관
